'''Helen Sedgwick''' is an author of literary fiction, science fiction and crime, a literary editor, and a research physicist.<ref>Author Interviews, [https://authorinterviews.co.uk/author/helen-sedgwick/  Helen Sedgwick], ''authorinterviews.co.uk'' (2019)</ref>

== Life ==

Sedgwick was born in London and studied [[physics]] at the [[University of Bristol]].<ref>Scotsman, [https://www.scotsman.com/whats-on/arts-and-entertainment/helen-sedgwick-discusses-her-first-novel-1469632/ Helen Sedgwick discusses her first novel], ''www.scotsman.com'', Aug 16 (2016)</ref> She gained a PhD in physics from the [[University of Edinburgh]]<ref>Edinburgh International Book Festival [https://www.edbookfest.co.uk/writers/helen-sedgwick-1/ Author biography], ''www.edbookfest.co.uk'' (2016)</ref> and an MLitt in Creative Writing from the [[University of Glasgow]].<ref>[https://www.gla.ac.uk/subjects/creativewriting/alumni/ Glasgow University Alumni], ''www.gla.ac.uk''</ref>

After leaving physics research to become a freelance writer,<ref>BBC, [https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b01qsv0w Helen Sedgwick biography], ''www.bbc.co.uk'', Feb 24 (2013)</ref> Sedgwick worked as the joint managing director of Cargo Publishing from 2014 to 2015,<ref>The Bookseller, [https://www.thebookseller.com/news/tasker-and-sedgwick-become-cargo-joint-mds/ Tasker and Sedgwick become Cargo joint MDs], ''www.thebookseller.com'', March 12 (2014)</ref> Sedgwick was also the managing editor of [[Gutter magazine]] and worked as a creative writing tutor.<ref>Scottish Book trust [https://www.scottishbooktrust.com/authors/helen-sedgwick/ Helen Sedgwick on the Live Literature Database], ''www.scottishbooktrust.com''</ref>

She released her first novel in 2016, ''The Comet Seekers''.<ref>The New York Times Book Review, [http://www.nytimes.com/2016/12/02/books/review/a-ghost-story-leaps-through-time-and-space.html?_r=0 The Comet Seekers: A ghost story leaps through time and space], www.nytimes.com, Dec 2 (2016)</ref><ref>The Herald, [https://www.heraldscotland.com/arts_ents/14736415.face-to-face-author-helen-sedgwick-on-her-first-novel-the-comet-seekers-and-the-consoling-scale-of-the-universe/ Face to Face: Author Helen Sedgwick on her first novel The Comet Seekers and the consoling scale of the universe], ''www.heraldscotland.com'', Sept 12 (2016)</ref><ref>The Irish Times, [https://www.irishtimes.com/culture/books/the-comet-seekers-review-the-patterns-in-the-stars-1.2771924 The Comet Seekers Review: The Patterns In The Stars], www.irishtimes.com, Aug 29 (2016)</ref> This was followed by her second novel, ''The Growing Season'',<ref>The Guardian, [https://www.theguardian.com/books/2017/sep/29/ The Growing Season Review], www.theguardian.com, Sept 29 (2017)</ref> which was shortlisted for Fiction Book of the Year in Scotland's National Book Awards 2018.<ref>Scottish Review of Books, [https://www.scottishreviewofbooks.org/free-content/saltire-shortlists-showcase-emerging-talents-alongside-household-names/ Saltire Literary Awards Shortlist Announced], ''www.scottishreviewofbooks.org'' Oct 23 (2018)</ref> Sedgwick's first crime novel was ''When The Dead Come Calling'',<ref>The Scotsman, [https://www.scotsman.com/arts-and-culture/books/book-review-when-dead-come-calling-helen-sedgwick-1395157 Book Review: When The Dead Come Calling], www.scotsman.com, Feb 4 (2020)</ref> the opening book in the Burrowhead Mysteries crime trilogy.<ref>The Bookseller, [https://www.thebookseller.com/news/atmospheric-crime-trilogy-point-blank-743021 Sedgwick's Atmospheric Crime Trilogy to Point Blank], ''www.thebookseller.com'' March 1 (2018)</ref> She cites her scientific background as a big influence on her writing.<ref>BBC Radio 4, [https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b07q2dn4 Helen Sedgwick on Woman's Hour], ''www.bbc.co.uk'' (2016)</ref>

Sedgwick is a member of The [[Society of Authors]]<ref>The Society of Authors [https://www.societyofauthors.org/writer-Profile?itemID=7477/ Helen Sedgwick], ''www.societyofauthors.org''</ref> and the [[Crime Writers' Association]].<ref>The Crime Writers Association [https://thecwa.co.uk/find-an-author/sedgwick-helen Helen Sedgwick], ''thecwa.co.uk''</ref> She lives in Tain, in [[Ross-shire]] in the [[Scottish Highlands]]<ref>Ross-shire Journal, [https://www.whatson-north.co.uk/whats-on/books/sea-change-for-novelist-helen-sedgwick-who-publishes-her-crime-novel-debut-189016/ Seven Days Guide], ''www.whatson-north.co.uk'', Jan 3 (2020)</ref> with her partner and their daughter.<ref>Crime Review [https://www.crimereview.co.uk/page.php/interview/8314 Countdown with Helen Sedgwick], ''www.crimereview.co.uk'' (2020)</ref>

== Awards ==

*2012 Scottish Book Trust New Writers Award.<ref>Scottish Book Trust [https://www.scottishbooktrust.com/writing-and-authors/new-writers-awards/previous-new-writers-awardees/ New Writers Awardees], ''www.scottishbooktrust.com'' (2012)</ref>
*2016 Glamour Book of the Year: ''The Comet Seekers''.<ref>Glamour, [https://www.glamourmagazine.co.uk/gallery/the-10-best-books-of-2016 The 10 Best Novels of 2016], ''www.glamourmagazine.co.uk'' Dec 2 (2016)</ref>
*2016 Waterstones Scottish Book of the Month: ''The Comet Seekers''.
*2018 Scotland's National Book Awards Fiction Book of the Year shortlist: ''The Growing Season''.<ref>Saltire Society [https://www.saltiresociety.org.uk/news/2018/10/22/2018-saltire-literary-awards-shortlist-unveiled-at-special-event-in-edinburgh/ 2018 shortlist] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201019134037/https://www.saltiresociety.org.uk/news/2018/10/22/2018-saltire-literary-awards-shortlist-unveiled-at-special-event-in-edinburgh |date=19 October 2020 }}, www.saltiresociety.org.uk (2018)</ref>
*2021 Dr Gavin Wallace Fellowship.<ref>Creative Scotland [https://www.creativescotland.com/what-we-do/latest-news/archive/2021/07/helen-sedgwick-appointed-2021-dr-gavin-wallace-fellow Helen Sedgwick appointed 2021 Dr Gavin Wallace Fellow], www.creativescotland.com (2021)</ref>
